summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic graft-versus-host disease, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted with worsening perianal pain following a recent hospitalization for gastrointestinal symptoms. He was found to have a perirectal abscess, confirmed on physical examination, and underwent examination under anesthesia with incision and drainage. A Malecot drain was placed for ongoing irrigation. Cultures from the abscess grew Group B Streptococcus and Bacteroides fragilis group. He received 24 hours of intravenous antibiotics followed by oral therapy. His condition stabilized quickly, and he was discharged home with visiting nursing support for wound care, instructions to continue all baseline medications plus antibiotics, and plans for follow-up with surgery and oncology. The hospital stay was brief and uncomplicated.
